# Q-Pass Android App (APK) Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** A downloadable Android app (`.apk`, and optionally a Play Store listing) that opens Q-Pass full screen, with its own icon, without the browser address bar.

**Architecture:** A Trusted Web Activity (TWA): a thin Android shell, generated by Google's Bubblewrap tool from the site's existing web app manifest, that shows the live site in Chrome full screen. The app holds no app code of its own, so every Vercel deploy updates the app's contents; the APK is rebuilt only when its name, icon, package ID or domain change. The site proves it owns the app with a Digital Asset Links file (`/.well-known/assetlinks.json`); without it Android shows an address bar.

**Tech Stack:** `@bubblewrap/cli` (installs its own JDK 17 and Android SDK on first run), the existing `src/app/manifest.ts` and `public/icon-*.png`, Vitest for the asset-links check.

**Spec:** this document. The installable web app it builds on is already on `main` (commits `51169c5`, `8476e9f`).

## Decisions to make before Task 1

These are hard or impossible to change once phones have the app. Write the answers here before starting.

| # | Decision | Options | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | How people get the app | **A.** Send the `.apk` file directly (free; each phone allows "Install unknown apps" once). **B.** Google Play Store (one-time US$25 developer account; review takes days). | Start with **A** for the team; add **B** later if needed. Bubblewrap builds both files from one setup. |
| D2 | Package ID (permanent app identity) | Reverse-domain, lowercase, e.g. `org.tac.qpass` | Pick one the church controls. It can never change for installed or Play Store apps. |
| D3 | Domain the app opens | `q-pass-code.vercel.app` or a custom domain (e.g. `qpass.<church>.org`) | Decide **before** building: the app and its asset-links file are tied to one domain, and changing it means a new APK on every phone. A custom domain survives a Vercel project rename. |
| D4 | Who keeps the signing key | One named person plus a backup (password manager and an offline copy) | Required. A lost key means no updates: every phone must uninstall and reinstall a new app. |

## Global Constraints

- The signing keystore and its passwords are **never committed**. They live outside the repo (Task 1 uses `../../q-pass-keys/` relative to `android/`).
- Every build is signed with the **same keystore**, forever.
- App name `Q-Pass`, launcher name `Q-Pass`, theme and background colour `#1b1c1f`, start URL `/`: the same values as `src/app/manifest.ts`.
- Icons: `https://<D3 domain>/icon-512.png` (launcher) and `https://<D3 domain>/icon-maskable-512.png` (maskable).
- `public/.well-known/assetlinks.json` must list the SHA-256 fingerprint of **every** key that signs a build users get: the upload key, plus Google's app-signing key if D1 = B.
- Phones need Chrome installed and enabled. A TWA runs in Chrome.

## Review Focus

- **Asset links don't match** (wrong package ID, fingerprint or domain): the app opens but shows an address bar along the top. Task 2's test pins the file's shape, and Task 3 step 2 checks it on a phone.
- **Play Store build without Google's fingerprint** (D1 = B): Play users see an address bar even though the sideloaded APK looks fine. Task 4B step 3 adds the second fingerprint.
- **Camera permission refused inside the app:** the scanner must show its existing "Camera is blocked or unavailable…" message and the "Type a ticket number" fallback, not a blank screen. Checked in Task 3 step 4.
- **No internet when the app opens:** with no service worker, Chrome shows its offline page. Expected for now; scans made while already open still queue (existing `src/lib/offline.ts`). Checked in Task 3 step 6 so nobody mistakes it for a crash.
- **"Install Q-Pass" button inside the app:** it must not show (Chrome sends no install offer inside an installed app). Checked in Task 3 step 3.

---

### Task 1: Generate and build the Android app

**Files:**
- Create: `android/twa-manifest.json` (Bubblewrap's settings, committed so builds are repeatable)
- Create: `android/.gitignore`
- Generated, not committed: the rest of `android/` (Gradle project, `*.apk`, `*.aab`)
- Outside the repo: `../q-pass-keys/q-pass.keystore` (relative to the repo root)

**Interfaces:**
- Produces: `android/app-release-signed.apk`, `android/app-release-bundle.aab`, and the upload key's SHA-256 fingerprint (`AA:BB:…`, 32 colon-separated hex pairs), used by Task 2.

- [ ] **Step 1: Install Bubblewrap.** Run `npm i -g @bubblewrap/cli`. On first use it offers to download JDK 17 and the Android SDK into `~/.bubblewrap`; accept both (the machine's Java 21 is not the version it expects).
- [ ] **Step 2: Initialise from the live manifest.** From the repo root, run `mkdir android && cd android && bubblewrap init --manifest https://<D3 domain>/manifest.webmanifest`. Answer with the Global Constraints values, package ID = D2, key path `../../q-pass-keys/q-pass.keystore`, key alias `qpass`. Let it create the key, and save both passwords in the password manager straight away (D4).
- [ ] **Step 3: Ignore everything except the settings file.** Write `android/.gitignore`:
  ```gitignore
  *
  !.gitignore
  !twa-manifest.json
  ```
- [ ] **Step 4: Build.** Run `bubblewrap build` in `android/`. Expected: `app-release-signed.apk` and `app-release-bundle.aab` created, with no errors.
- [ ] **Step 5: Record the fingerprint.** Run `keytool -list -v -keystore ../../q-pass-keys/q-pass.keystore -alias qpass` and copy the `SHA256:` line into D4's password-manager entry and into Task 2.
- [ ] **Step 6: Commit.**
  ```bash
  git add android/.gitignore android/twa-manifest.json
  git commit -m "build(android): Bubblewrap settings for the Q-Pass app"
  ```
  Check `git status` shows no `.apk`, `.aab` or `.keystore` files staged.

### Task 2: Prove the site owns the app (Digital Asset Links)

**Files:**
- Create: `public/.well-known/assetlinks.json`
- Test: `src/lib/assetlinks.test.ts`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: package ID (D2) and the SHA-256 fingerprint from Task 1 step 5.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing test** in `src/lib/assetlinks.test.ts`. It reads `public/.well-known/assetlinks.json` and asserts:
  ```ts
  expect(links).toHaveLength(1)
  expect(links[0].relation).toEqual(['delegate_permission/common.handle_all_urls'])
  expect(links[0].target.namespace).toBe('android_app')
  expect(links[0].target.package_name).toBe('<D2 package ID>')
  expect(links[0].target.sha256_cert_fingerprints.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)
  for (const f of links[0].target.sha256_cert_fingerprints) expect(f).toMatch(/^([0-9A-F]{2}:){31}[0-9A-F]{2}$/)
  ```
- [ ] **Step 2: Run it and see it fail.** Run `npx vitest run src/lib/assetlinks.test.ts`. Expected: FAIL (file not found).
- [ ] **Step 3: Create `public/.well-known/assetlinks.json`:** one statement with the relation, namespace and package ID asserted above, and `sha256_cert_fingerprints: ["<Task 1 step 5 value>"]`.
- [ ] **Step 4: Run the tests.** Run `npx vitest run`. Expected: all pass, including the new test.
- [ ] **Step 5: Check it's served.** With `npm run dev` running, `curl -i http://localhost:3000/.well-known/assetlinks.json` returns `200`, a JSON content type and the file. It must load without signing in.
- [ ] **Step 6: Commit and deploy.** `git add public/.well-known/assetlinks.json src/lib/assetlinks.test.ts`, commit `feat(android): digital asset links for the Q-Pass app`, then push to `main`.
- [ ] **Step 7: Check Google sees it.** Open `https://digitalassetlinks.googleapis.com/v1/statements:list?source.web.site=https://<D3 domain>&relation=delegate_permission/common.handle_all_urls`. Expected: one statement with the package ID and fingerprint.

### Task 3: Try it on real phones

No code. Install `android/app-release-signed.apk` on at least two Android phones (one older or slower), using a USB cable (`adb install app-release-signed.apk`) or by sending the file. Use a different browser profile from any earlier "Install Q-Pass" test, or uninstall that first.

- [ ] **Step 1:** The app installs, and its icon and name show as Q-Pass in the app drawer.
- [ ] **Step 2:** It opens full screen with **no address bar**. If a bar shows, re-check Task 2 (package ID, fingerprint, domain) and Google's checker before anything else.
- [ ] **Step 3:** Sign in as a volunteer: the scanner opens and **no "Install Q-Pass" button** shows (sign-in page and account menu).
- [ ] **Step 4:** Camera: allow it and scan a real ticket (green or red card). Then refuse camera access in Android settings, reopen, and check for the "Camera is blocked or unavailable…" message and that typing a ticket number works.
- [ ] **Step 5:** Flashlight button (top-right of the camera) toggles the light, the 5-second countdown works, and the phone's Back button behaves sensibly.
- [ ] **Step 6:** Airplane mode while the app is open: scanning shows "Saved offline". Opening the app from cold in airplane mode shows Chrome's offline page (expected; see Review Focus).
- [ ] **Step 7:** Sign in as an admin: the desk, tickets and QR code pages work, and downloads (CSV, QR zip) save to the phone.

### Task 4A: Share the APK directly (D1 = A)

- [ ] **Step 1:** Upload `app-release-signed.apk` somewhere staff can download it (a shared Drive folder, or the church's site). Keep only the latest version there.
- [ ] **Step 2:** Write the three-line instruction to send with the link: download, allow "Install unknown apps" for the browser or Files app when asked, then open Q-Pass.
- [ ] **Step 3:** Test the download link on a phone that has never had Q-Pass.

### Task 4B: Google Play Store (D1 = B)

- [ ] **Step 1:** Create the Play Console developer account (one-time US$25) and the app listing (name, short description, the 512 icon, phone screenshots, privacy policy URL).
- [ ] **Step 2:** Upload `app-release-bundle.aab` to the **Internal testing** track, with Play App Signing on.
- [ ] **Step 3:** In Play Console → App integrity, copy **Google's app-signing SHA-256**. Add it as a second entry in `sha256_cert_fingerprints` (Task 2 file), run `npx vitest run`, commit, push, and repeat Task 2 step 7.
- [ ] **Step 4:** Install from the internal testing link and repeat Task 3 steps 1–2. Only then promote to Production.

### Task 5: Updating the app later (reference)

- **Web changes** (most changes): deploy to Vercel as usual. The app shows them next time it opens; no rebuild.
- **App name, icon, colours or domain changes:** in `android/`, raise `appVersionCode` (and `appVersionName`) in `twa-manifest.json`, run `bubblewrap update` then `bubblewrap build` with the **same keystore**, commit `twa-manifest.json`, and redistribute (4A) or upload the new `.aab` (4B).
- **Domain change** (D3): also update `public/.well-known/assetlinks.json` on the new domain before shipping the new APK.
